title: Hagar
lead: Sarah's Egyptian slave woman, given to Abraham as a second wife, who bore Ishmael. She ran away from harsh treatment and was later driven out with her son, and both times God met her in the desert. She is the first person in the Bible to give God a name (Genesis 16:13); Paul uses her as a figure of slavery (Galatians 4:21–31), and in Islam she is honored as the mother of Ishmael.

sections.b: Outside Genesis the Bible names Hagar only in Galatians, where Paul makes her and Sarah two covenants: Hagar stands for Mount Sinai and slavery, Sarah for the free Jerusalem above (Galatians 4:21–31). Her son's descendants appear as the "Hagrites" east of the Jordan (1 Chronicles 5:10, 19–20; Psalm 83:6). In Islam, Hajar's search for water and the spring of Zamzam are remembered in the pilgrimage to Mecca, and in modern womanist theology she is a figure of survival under oppression.
